docs.title: AI Codebase Knowledge Builder
docs.text: Ever stared at a new codebase written by others feeling completely lost? This project analyzes GitHub repositories and creates beginner-friendly tutorials explaining exactly how the code works - all powered by AI! Our intelligent system automatically breaks down complex codebases into digestible explanations that even beginners can understand.

docs.title: 🚀 Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Clone this repository 

    git clone https://github.com/ardennguyen/Codebase-Knowledge-Builder

  2. Install dependencies (we highly recommend using a virtual environment of your choice like venv, conda, uv, or pyenv to avoid polluting your global system): 

    pip install -r requirements.txt

  3. Set up LLM in utils/call_llm.py by providing credentials via a .env file. You can use native Gemini by setting GEMINI_API_KEY. For OpenRouter, set LLM_PROVIDER=OPENROUTER and OPENROUTER_API_KEY.

  4. Generate a complete codebase tutorial by running the main script: 

    # Analyze a GitHub repository
python main.py --repo https://github.com/username/repo --include "*.py" "*.js" --exclude "tests/*" --max-size 50000

# Or, analyze a local directory
python main.py --dir /path/to/your/codebase --include "*.py" --exclude "*test*"

# Or, generate a tutorial in Vietnamese
python main.py --repo https://github.com/username/repo --language "Vietnamese"

docs.title: CLI Options
docs.text:
• --repo or --dir - Specify either a GitHub repo URL or a local directory path (required, mutually exclusive)
  • -n, --name - Project name (optional, derived from URL/directory if omitted)
  • -t, --token - GitHub token (or set GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable)
  • -o, --output - Output directory (default: ./output)
  • -i, --include - Files to include (e.g., *.py *.js). Defaults to * (all files).
  • -e, --exclude - Files to exclude. Custom patterns are automatically merged with a massive global exclusion list (build caches, node_modules, binaries, media, AI environments) AND your repository's native .gitignore rules.
  • -s, --max-size - Maximum file size in bytes (default: 200KB)
  • --language - Language for the generated tutorial (default: "english")
  • --max-abstractions - Maximum number of abstractions to identify (default: 10)
  • --no-cache - Disable LLM response caching (default: caching enabled)
  • --thinking-level - Thinking effort level for native Gemini, OpenRouter, and Ollama reasoning models (e.g., low, medium, high). Leave empty to use model defaults.
  • --max-tokens - Maximum number of tokens for the context window (default: fetched dynamically from the model).
  • --mode - Documentation style (tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk). (default: tutorial)
  • --advanced - Legacy flag: equivalent to --mode advanced
  • --mkdocs - Format output for MkDocs Material (adds YAML frontmatter & nav snippet)
  • --incremental - Enable MD5 incremental caching to skip unchanged modules (Only supported in --mode api-reference)
  • --force-rebuild - Clear incremental cache and regenerate all chapters from scratch (use with --incremental)
  • --batch - Maximum files per batch when using map-reduce mode (default: 50).
  • --force-batch - Force the pipeline to use map-reduce mode regardless of context limits.
  • --debug - Enable verbose debug output.
  • --cleanup - Clean up logs and cache JSON at the end of the script (default: No).

The application will crawl the repository, analyze the codebase structure, generate tutorial content in the specified language, and save the output in the specified directory (default: ./output). This includes individual chapter files, an index.md, and a compiled full_content.md containing the complete tutorial with a Table of Contents.

Built using Pocket Flow, a 100-line LLM framework.

docs.title: 1. Requirements
docs.text:
Notes for AI: Keep it simple and clear. If the requirements are abstract, write concrete user stories

User Story: As a developer onboarding to a new codebase, I want a tutorial automatically generated from its GitHub repository or local directory, optionally in a specific language. The system supports four documentation styles: a tutorial mode that explains core abstractions with beginner-friendly language, analogies, and code walkthroughs; an advanced mode that produces architecture deep-dives aimed at senior developers or PMs joining a project mid-way, covering design patterns, key dependencies, and practical onboarding notes; an api-reference mode that generates exhaustive, formal API documentation for every code module (1:1 file-to-chapter mapping); and an sdk mode that produces SDK-style integration guides. The system must also gracefully handle codebases of any size by dynamically switching to a Map-Reduce approach when context limits are reached.

Input: - A publicly accessible GitHub repository URL or a local directory path. - A project name (optional, will be derived from the URL/directory if not provided). - Desired language for the tutorial (optional, defaults to English). - Advanced configurations: documentation style (--mode), token scaling (--max-tokens, --batch, --force-batch), prompting (--thinking-level, --max-abstractions), caching (--no-cache), output format (--mkdocs, --incremental), debugging (--debug), and execution cleanup (--cleanup).

Output: - A directory named after the project containing: - An index.md file with: - A high-level project summary (potentially translated). - A Mermaid flowchart diagram visualizing relationships between abstractions (using potentially translated names/labels). - An ordered list of links to chapter files (using potentially translated names). - A link to full_content.md at the bottom. - Individual Markdown files for each chapter (01_chapter_one.md, 02_chapter_two.md, etc.) detailing core abstractions in a logical order (potentially translated content). - A full_content.md (inside the project subdirectory) containing all merged chapters and a Table of Contents. - When --mkdocs is used: YAML frontmatter is injected into every chapter, filenames mirror source directory structure instead of numbered prefixes, and a nav_snippet.yml navigation file is generated for MkDocs integration. - When --incremental is used (api-reference mode only): a .doc_cache_manifest.json tracks MD5 hashes of source files to skip regeneration of unchanged modules across runs.

docs.title: 2. Flow Design
docs.text: Notes for AI: 1. Consider the design patterns of agent, map-reduce, rag, and workflow. Apply them if they fit. 2. Present a concise, high-level description of the workflow.

docs.title: Applicable Design Pattern:
docs.text:
This project primarily uses a Workflow pattern with dynamic branching into a Map-Reduce pattern. The chapter writing step also utilizes a BatchNode.

  1. Workflow & Routing: The overall process fetches code, estimates token payloads, and routes based on context limits. If the codebase fits the LLM window, it goes directly to abstraction identification.
  2. Map-Reduce: If the codebase exceeds context limits (or if forced), the codebase is grouped into token-aware, directory-isolated batches (each batch stays under the effective token limit and never mixes files from different directories). A MapAbstractions BatchNode processes each batch individually, and a ReduceAbstractions Node merges them into a global list.
  3. Batch Processing: The WriteChapters node processes each identified abstraction independently (map) before final tutorial compilation.

docs.title: Flow high-level Design:
docs.text:
1. FetchRepo: Crawls the specified repository/directory using crawl_github_files or crawl_local_files.
  2. ContextRouter: Analyzes the total token payload of the fetched files using tiktoken. Dynamically calculates prompt overhead (template tokens + directory tree tokens) and computes an effective limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead. If --mode api-reference is used, routes to "deterministic". If the file content tokens exceed this effective limit or if --force-batch is used, it chunks files into token-aware, directory-isolated batches (never mixing files from different directories) and routes to "batch". Also builds a compact directory tree of all files (stored in shared["directory_tree"]) for cross-batch awareness. With --debug, displays detailed per-batch file lists and token breakdowns. Otherwise, it routes to "direct".
  3. Path A: Direct
    • IdentifyAbstractions: Analyzes the entire codebase at once to identify core abstractions.
  4. Path B: Map-Reduce
    • MapAbstractions (BatchNode): Analyzes each localized directory chunk to extract partial abstractions. Each batch receives the full directory tree for cross-batch awareness.
    • ReduceAbstractions: Merges overlapping/partial abstractions into a global list of architecture components.
  5. Path C: Deterministic (api-reference mode)
    • DeterministicFileMapper: Bypasses LLM-based abstraction discovery entirely. Uses a lightweight LLM call to filter out non-code files (configs, UI layouts, static assets), then creates a 1:1 mapping of each code file to a documentation module. Skips AnalyzeRelationships and OrderChapters, routing directly to WriteChapters.
  6. AnalyzeRelationships (Paths A & B only): Takes the unified abstractions list (from either path) and generates a high-level project summary and relationships diagram. Uses token-budget-aware file inclusion: the budget is split evenly across abstractions, with unused budget redistributed in a second pass, maximizing code context without exceeding the context window.
  7. OrderChapters (Paths A & B only): Determines the most logical sequence to present the abstractions.
  8. WriteChapters (BatchNode): Iterates through the ordered abstractions and writes detailed Markdown chapters using context-aware code inclusion.
  9. CombineTutorial: Assembles the final outputs including index.md, individual chapter files, and a compiled full_content.md.
flowchart TD
    A[FetchRepo] --> Router[ContextRouter]

    Router -->|direct| B[IdentifyAbstractions]
    Router -->|batch| M1[MapAbstractions]
    Router -->|deterministic| DFM[DeterministicFileMapper]
    M1 --> M2[ReduceAbstractions]

    B --> C[AnalyzeRelationships]
    M2 --> C

    C --> D[OrderChapters]
    D --> E[Batch WriteChapters]
    DFM --> E
    E --> F[CombineTutorial]

def crawl_local_files(directory, include_patterns=None, exclude_patterns=None,
                      max_file_size=None, use_relative_paths=True) -> dict:
    # Returns: {"files": {relative_path_str: content_str, ...}}

Directory Pruning Algorithm (critical for nested directories like Core.User/.vs/): 

# During os.walk, for each subdirectory d:
excluded_dirs = set()
for d in dirs:
    dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), directory)
    # Check .gitignore first
    if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
        excluded_dirs.add(d)
        continue
    # Check exclude patterns — strip trailing /* for directory matching
    if exclude_patterns:
        for pattern in exclude_patterns:
            dir_pattern = pattern[:-2] if pattern.endswith("/*") else pattern
            if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                break
# Remove matched dirs to prevent os.walk descent
for d in dirs.copy():
    if d in excluded_dirs:
        dirs.remove(d)

Note: Directory validation: raises ValueError if directory path doesn't exist. Loads .gitignore with utf-8-sig encoding (BOM-safe). All directories and files are sorted() for deterministic traversal order.

Progress Display Format: - Green (\033[92m): [processed] — Successfully read files - Gray (\033[90m): [excluded (.gitignore)] / [excluded (not in include list)] — Skipped by pattern - Red (\033[91m): [size limit: {size_kb:.0f}KB] — Exceeded max_file_size - Red (\033[91m): [cannot process: not a text file] / [cannot process: {e}] — Binary/encoding errors

Note: After crawling, prints a --- Crawl Summary --- block with total found, processed, excluded, size limited, and non-text counts.

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdirname:
    print(f"Cloning SSH repo {repo_url} to temp dir {tmpdirname} ...")
    try:
        repo = git.Repo.clone_from(repo_url, tmpdirname)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"Error cloning repo: {e}")
        return {"files": {}, "stats": {"error": str(e)}}

    files = {}
    skipped_files = []

    # --- ANSI colors ---
    C_GREEN  = "\033[92m"
    C_GRAY   = "\033[90m"
    C_RED    = "\033[91m"
    C_RESET  = "\033[0m"

    # --- Counters ---
    count_processed = 0
    count_excluded = 0
    count_size_limit = 0
    count_non_text = 0
    skipped_size_list = []
    skipped_non_text_list = []
    entry_num = 0

    # --- Load .gitignore (BOM-safe) ---
    gitignore_path = os.path.join(tmpdirname, ".gitignore")
    gitignore_spec = None
    if os.path.exists(gitignore_path):
        try:
            with open(gitignore_path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                gitignore_spec = pathspec.PathSpec.from_lines("gitwildmatch", f.readlines())
        except Exception:
            pass

    for root, dirs, filenames in os.walk(tmpdirname):
        # --- Directory pruning (same algorithm as crawl_local_files) ---
        excluded_dirs = set()
        for d in sorted(dirs):
            dirpath_rel = os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root, d), tmpdirname)
            reason = None
            if gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(dirpath_rel):
                reason = "excluded (.gitignore)"
            elif exclude_patterns:
                for pattern in exclude_patterns:
                    dir_pattern = pattern[:-2] if pattern.endswith("/*") else pattern
                    if fnmatch.fnmatch(dirpath_rel, dir_pattern) or fnmatch.fnmatch(d, dir_pattern):
                        reason = "excluded"
                        break
            if reason:
                excluded_dirs.add(d)
                entry_num += 1
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {dirpath_rel}/ [{reason}]{C_RESET}")

        for d in dirs.copy():
            if d in excluded_dirs:
                dirs.remove(d)
        dirs.sort()  # Deterministic traversal order

        # --- File processing ---
        for filename in sorted(filenames):
            abs_path = os.path.join(root, filename)
            rel_path = os.path.relpath(abs_path, tmpdirname)
            entry_num += 1

            if not should_include_file(rel_path, filename, gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
                count_excluded += 1
                print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [excluded]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            try:
                file_size = os.path.getsize(abs_path)
            except OSError:
                continue

            if file_size > max_file_size:
                count_size_limit += 1
                skipped_size_list.append(rel_path)
                size_kb = file_size / 1024
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [size limit: {size_kb:.0f}KB]{C_RESET}")
                continue

            try:
                with open(abs_path, "r", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                    content = f.read()
                files[rel_path] = content
                count_processed += 1
                print(f"{C_GREEN}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [processed]{C_RESET}")
            except (UnicodeDecodeError, ValueError):
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [cannot process: not a text file]{C_RESET}")
            except Exception as e:
                count_non_text += 1
                skipped_non_text_list.append(rel_path)
                print(f"{C_RED}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [cannot process: {e}]{C_RESET}")

    # --- Crawl Summary ---
    total_fetched = count_processed + count_excluded + count_size_limit + count_non_text
    print(f"\n--- Crawl Summary ---")
    print(f"  Total found : {total_fetched}")
    print(f"{C_GREEN}  Processed   : {count_processed}{C_RESET}")
    if count_excluded > 0:
        print(f"{C_GRAY}  Excluded    : {count_excluded}{C_RESET}")
    if count_size_limit > 0:
        print(f"{C_RED}  Size limit  : {count_size_limit}{C_RESET}")
        for sf in skipped_size_list:
            print(f"{C_RED}    - {sf}{C_RESET}")
    if count_non_text > 0:
        print(f"{C_RED}  Non-text    : {count_non_text}{C_RESET}")
        for sf in skipped_non_text_list:
            print(f"{C_RED}    - {sf}{C_RESET}")
    print(f"---------------------")

    return {
        "files": files,
        "stats": {
            "downloaded_count": len(files),
            "skipped_count": len(skipped_files),
            "skipped_files": skipped_files,
            "base_path": None,
            "include_patterns": include_patterns,
            "exclude_patterns": exclude_patterns,
            "source": "ssh_clone"
        }
    }

Step 2 — Dynamic Branch Detection (handles multi-segment branch names like feature/foo): 

if len(path_parts) > 2 and 'tree' == path_parts[2]:

else:

Step 4 — Recursive Content Fetching (1 API call per directory): 

def fetch_contents(path):
    url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}"
    params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}
    response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=(30, 30))

    # Rate limit handling with header-based wait:
    if response.status_code in (403, 429) and 'rate limit exceeded' in response.text.lower():
        if not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Provide a token.")
        reset_time = int(response.headers.get('X-RateLimit-Reset', 0))
        wait_time = max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1
        time.sleep(wait_time)
        return fetch_contents(path)  # Recursive retry

    contents = response.json()
    if not isinstance(contents, list):
        contents = [contents]

    for item in contents:
        if item["type"] == "file":
            # Check patterns, size, then fetch content
            # Path A: Use download_url directly, check Content-Length header
            # Path B (fallback): If no download_url, GET item["url"],
            #   base64 decode with size estimate: len(content) * 0.75 > max_file_size
        elif item["type"] == "dir":
            # Check gitignore + exclude before recursing
            fetch_contents(item["path"])

Step 5 — Dual Content Fetch Strategy: 

# Path A: download_url available
if "download_url" in item and item["download_url"]:
    file_response = requests.get(item["download_url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
    content_length = int(file_response.headers.get('content-length', 0))
    if content_length > max_file_size:  # Final size check
        continue
    files[rel_path] = file_response.text

# Path B: base64 fallback
else:
    content_response = requests.get(item["url"], headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))
    content_data = content_response.json()
    if len(content_data["content"]) * 0.75 > max_file_size:  # Approximate size
        continue
    file_content = base64.b64decode(content_data["content"]).decode('utf-8')
    files[rel_path] = file_content

No LLM call. Routes to "direct" or "batch". Writes shared["max_tokens"], shared["file_batches"], shared["directory_tree"].

ContextRouter Algorithm: 1. Auto-detect max_tokens from provider if not set; write to shared["max_tokens"] 2. Measure prompt overhead = max(template_tokens for tutorial/advanced map_abstractions.md) + directory_tree_tokens 3. safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95); effective_limit = safety_limit - prompt_overhead 4. Count total file content tokens using f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n" per file 5. If total_tokens > effective_limit OR force_batch: - Group files by os.path.dirname(path) — NEVER mix directories - Within each directory group, create batches respecting both effective_limit tokens AND batch_size file count - Return "batch" 6. Else: Return "direct"

other_dir/

def create_token_counter():

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The flow.py module defines the workflow orchestration layer of the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder system. It constructs a declarative directed acyclic graph (DAG) using the pocketflow framework to automate the end-to-end extraction, analysis, structuring, and synthesis of codebase documentation and tutorials.

The module provides a single factory function, create_tutorial_flow(), which initializes pipeline execution nodes defined in nodes and wires them together with deterministic and conditional branching edges. The pipeline dynamically routes execution based on repository token limits and processing strategies, handling three distinct architectural workflows:

  1. Direct Path: For smaller codebases that fit within standard context windows, routing directly to single-pass abstraction identification.
  2. Batch (Map-Reduce) Path: For large repositories that exceed token limits, breaking files into chunks, mapping abstractions in parallel/batches, and reducing them into a unified concept list.
  3. Deterministic Path: For structured 1:1 file-to-chapter generation, bypassing dynamic concept discovery to build dedicated documentation chapters per source file.

docs.title: create_tutorial_flow()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def create_tutorial_flow() -> Flow

Description: Instantiates and interconnects all execution nodes required to process a codebase into a cohesive multi-chapter tutorial. Nodes interacting with external Large Language Model (LLM) APIs are configured with exponential backoff and retry parameters (max_retries=5, wait=20) to ensure network resilience and handle API rate limits.

The pipeline defines directional connections using pocketflow's overloaded shift (>>) and minus (-) operators: * >> establishes an unconditional sequential transition between two nodes. * - "action" >> establishes a conditional transition triggered when the upstream node returns a specific routing action string ("direct", "batch", or "deterministic").

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * Flow: An initialized pocketflow.Flow instance configured with FetchRepo as its root entry node (start=fetch_repo).

Raises: * Does not raise exceptions during graph construction. Runtime exceptions during flow execution are managed by individual node retry policies and PocketFlow's execution runner.

Example: 

def create_tutorial_flow():
    fetch_repo = FetchRepo()
    context_router = ContextRouter()
    map_abstractions = MapAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    reduce_abstractions = ReduceAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    identify_abstractions = IdentifyAbstractions(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    analyze_relationships = AnalyzeRelationships(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    order_chapters = OrderChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    write_chapters = WriteChapters(max_retries=5, wait=20)
    combine_tutorial = CombineTutorial()
    deterministic_mapper = DeterministicFileMapper(max_retries=5, wait=20)

    fetch_repo >> context_router

    context_router - "direct" >> identify_abstractions
    context_router - "batch" >> map_abstractions
    context_router - "deterministic" >> deterministic_mapper

    map_abstractions >> reduce_abstractions

    identify_abstractions >> analyze_relationships
    reduce_abstractions >> analyze_relationships

    analyze_relationships >> order_chapters
    order_chapters >> write_chapters

    deterministic_mapper >> write_chapters

    write_chapters >> combine_tutorial

    return Flow(start=fetch_repo)

The function begins by instantiating the ingestion nodes: FetchRepo, which retrieves the target repository files (from either local storage or GitHub), and ContextRouter, which calculates total token volume to determine the processing strategy. It configures LLM-dependent nodes (MapAbstractions, ReduceAbstractions, IdentifyAbstractions, AnalyzeRelationships, OrderChapters, WriteChapters, DeterministicFileMapper) with a 5-retry limit and a 20-second wait interval between retries.

Next, it defines the routing branches using PocketFlow's syntax. ContextRouter evaluates the token context size and emits an action: * If "direct" is emitted, control transitions to IdentifyAbstractions, extracting high-level system components in a single prompt. * If "batch" is emitted, control transitions to MapAbstractions, which analyzes file subsets independently before forwarding results to ReduceAbstractions to synthesize overlapping abstractions. * If "deterministic" is emitted, control routes to DeterministicFileMapper to generate fixed chapter definitions mapping 1:1 with files in the codebase.

Following abstraction resolution, both the direct and batch branches converge at AnalyzeRelationships to generate cross-component dependency diagrams, followed by OrderChapters to sequence chapters pedagogically. Both the ordered dynamic chapters and deterministic file chapters flow into WriteChapters to draft full Markdown tutorials. Finally, WriteChapters streams its outputs into CombineTutorial, which assembles the complete index, navigations, and output documents.

The main.py script serves as the primary command-line interface (CLI) and runtime orchestrator for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder pipeline. It acts as the operational entry point that parses command-line parameters, loads environment variables via dotenv, sets up global default inclusion and exclusion file pattern registries, establishes shared memory state across processing nodes, and triggers execution of the tutorial generation pipeline defined in flow.

docs.text:
• Type: set[str]
  • Value: {"*"}
  • Description: The default wildcard matching rule applied during file discovery. By default, every file in the target repository or directory is considered for indexing unless filtered out by file size limits or exclusion lists.

docs.title: DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_PATTERNS
docs.text:
• Type: set[str]
  • Description: A comprehensive blacklist of glob patterns systematically skipped during repository traversal in both utils.crawl_github_files and utils.crawl_local_files. The set is categorized into seven distinct domains:
  • Media, Data, and Static Assets: Binary media, images, video, audio, office documents, and compressed archives (e.g., assets/*, *.png, *.pdf, *.zip, *.tar).
  • Build, Distribution, and Framework Caches: Compiled outputs and framework build directories (e.g., dist/*, build/*, target/*, .next/*, .nuxt/*, *.log, *.tmp).
  • Environments, Dependencies, and Lockfiles: Dependency installation folders and lockfiles across JavaScript, Python, Rust, Ruby, PHP, and Elixir (e.g., node_modules/*, venv/*, .venv/*, package-lock.json, Cargo.lock, poetry.lock).
  • Language-Specific Exclusions: Bytecode, coverage reports, compiled binaries, object files, and shared libraries (e.g., __pycache__/*, *.class, *.jar, *.o, *.dll, *.so, *.dylib).
  • OS and Version Control Metadata: VCS directories and operating system desktop metadata (e.g., .git/*, .github/*, .DS_Store, Thumbs.db).
  • Classic IDEs: IDE project settings and configuration files (e.g., .vscode/*, .idea/*, *.iml, .vs/*).
  • AI Agents and Modern AI IDEs: System configuration and scratchpads from modern AI coding assistants (e.g., .cursor/*, .windsurf/*, .cline/*, .roo/*, .agent/*, .continue/*, .gemini/*, .claude/*, .copilot/*).

docs.text:
# Resolve mode (backward compatibility for --advanced)
    doc_mode = "advanced" if args.advanced else args.mode

    # Enforce incremental cache constraints
    if args.incremental and doc_mode != "api-reference":
        print(
            "\n\033[93m[Warning] --incremental caching is only effective in 'api-reference' mode due to stable 1:1 file mapping. Disabling incremental cache for this run.\033[0m\n"
        )
        args.incremental = False

    # Handle --force-rebuild: delete the cache manifest to force fresh generation
    if args.force_rebuild and args.incremental:
        project_name = args.name
        if not project_name:
            # Derive project name the same way FetchRepo does
            if args.dir:
                project_name = os.path.basename(os.path.abspath(args.dir))
            elif args.repo:
                project_name = args.repo.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1]
        if project_name:
            output_base = args.output or "output"
            manifest_path = os.path.join(output_base, project_name, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
            if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
                os.remove(manifest_path)
                print(f"\033[93m[Force Rebuild] Deleted cache manifest: {manifest_path}\033[0m")
            else:
                print(f"\033[93m[Force Rebuild] No cache manifest found at {manifest_path} — all chapters will be generated fresh.\033[0m")
    elif args.force_rebuild and not args.incremental:
        print("\033[93m[Warning] --force-rebuild has no effect without --incremental. Ignoring.\033[0m")
This section normalizes legacy flags and validates incremental execution constraints. Because incremental MD5 checksum tracking relies on deterministic 1:1 source-to-chapter file mapping, --incremental is automatically disabled with a warning if used outside api-reference mode. If --force-rebuild is asserted in conjunction with --incremental, the existing .doc_cache_manifest.json file is located and deleted.

docs.title: get_content_for_indices()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_content_for_indices(files_data, indices) -> dict

Description: Extracts file content from the crawled file collection using a list of numerical indices, returning a dictionary mapping each index-annotated file path key (e.g., 0 # src/main.py) to its corresponding string payload.

Parameters: * files_data (list): Sequence of (path, content) tuples representing repository files. * indices (iterable): Collection of integer indices indicating which files to extract.

Returns: * dict: Key-value map where the key is formatted as "{i} # {path}" and the value is the raw file content string.

Raises: * None. Out-of-bounds indices are ignored via boundary checks (0 <= i < len(files_data)).

Example: 

def get_content_for_indices(files_data, indices):
    content_map = {}
    for i in indices:
        if 0 <= i < len(files_data):
            path, content = files_data[i]
            content_map[f"{i} # {path}"] = content  # Use index + path as key for context
    return content_map

This helper ensures safe indexed retrieval from the raw repository payload. By including the integer index in the dictionary key alongside the file path, downstream prompt builders can provide unambiguous cross-referencing information to the LLM.

docs.title: load_prompt_template()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def load_prompt_template(template_name: str, advanced_mode: bool = False, mode: str = None) -> str

Description: Locates, opens, and reads a Markdown-based prompt template file from the internal prompts/ directory tree based on the active mode (e.g., tutorial, advanced, api-reference, sdk).

Parameters: * template_name (str): Base name of the prompt template file (without .md). * advanced_mode (bool, optional): Legacy toggle for advanced mode. Defaults to False. * mode (str, optional): Target prompt subfolder override. Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: Raw template string decoded using utf-8-sig.

Raises: * FileNotFoundError: If the requested template markdown file does not exist under the resolved prompt directory.

Example: 

def load_prompt_template(template_name, advanced_mode=False, mode=None):
    """Load a prompt template file from the prompts/ directory."""
    if mode is None:
        prompt_dir = "advanced" if advanced_mode else "tutorial"
    else:
        prompt_dir = mode

    path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "prompts", prompt_dir, f"{template_name}.md")
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
        return f.read()

The function resolves relative pathing against the directory of nodes.py. Using utf-8-sig prevents byte-order mark issues when reading templates written or edited across different operating systems.

docs.title: parse_yaml_response()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def parse_yaml_response(response: str) -> object

Description: Extracts fenced YAML blocks (```yaml ... ```) from LLM output strings and parses them into native Python data structures using yaml.safe_load.

Parameters: * response (str): Raw string response returned by the language model.

Returns: * object: Parsed YAML structure (typically list or dict).

Raises: * ValueError: If no valid YAML block is fenced or if YAML parsing fails.

Example: 

def parse_yaml_response(response):
    """Extract and parse YAML from an LLM response fenced in ```yaml blocks."""
    try:
        yaml_str = response.strip().split("```yaml")[1].split("```")[0].strip()
        return yaml.safe_load(yaml_str)
    except Exception as e:
        raise ValueError(f"Failed to parse YAML: {e}") from e

This parser enforces a rigid structural contract with the LLM prompts. If the response contains markdown preamble or conversational text outside the fenced block, split("```yaml")[1].split("```")[0] isolates the payload. Any parsing syntax error is wrapped in a descriptive ValueError.

docs.title: create_token_counter()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def create_token_counter() -> callable

Description: Constructs a token-counting callable using tiktoken's cl100k_base encoding, falling back to a 4-character heuristic if the tokenizer cannot be initialized.

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * callable: A function accepting a string and returning an integer token count.

Raises: * None. Catches all exceptions to ensure fallback availability.

Example: 

def create_token_counter():
    """Create a token counting function using tiktoken with char-count fallback."""
    try:
        enc = tiktoken.get_encoding("cl100k_base")
        return lambda text: len(enc.encode(text, disallowed_special=()))
    except Exception:
        return lambda text: len(text) // 4

The counter is heavily utilized across prep methods for dynamic context budgeting. When evaluating large code payloads, disabling special token checks (disallowed_special=()) prevents crashes on arbitrary user source strings that happen to contain tokenizer control tokens.

docs.title: resolve_max_tokens()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def resolve_max_tokens(shared: dict) -> int

Description: Resolves the maximum input context length limit, reading from shared pipeline state or querying the provider-specific model context mapping via get_model_context_length.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared state dictionary passed across pipeline nodes.

Returns: * int: Maximum context window limit in tokens.

Raises: * None.

Example: 

def resolve_max_tokens(shared):
    """Resolve max_tokens from shared store or auto-detect from provider env vars."""
    max_tokens = shared.get("max_tokens")
    if max_tokens is not None:
        return max_tokens
    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if provider == "GEMINI" or not provider:
        endpoint = "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com"
        model_name = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")
        api_key = os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY", "")
    else:
        endpoint = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_BASE_URL", "")
        model_name = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", "")
        api_key = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_API_KEY", "")
    return get_model_context_length(endpoint, model_name, api_key)

The resolution checks for an explicit override in shared["max_tokens"] first. If omitted, it inspects environment variables (LLM_PROVIDER, GEMINI_MODEL, ${PROVIDER}_MODEL) and queries utils.call_llm.get_model_context_length to retrieve the active model's window capacity.

Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> dict

def prep(self, shared):

    local_dir = shared.get("local_dir")

Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> Union[str, list]

Description: Constructs token-aware file batches partitioned strictly by directory structure when batch mode is active, avoiding cross-directory mixing.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Unpacked values from prep().

Returns: * Union[str, list]: Route string ("direct" or "deterministic") or a list of batches [[(idx, path, content), ...], ...].

Example: 

def exec(self, prep_res):
    route, files_data, effective_limit, batch_size, file_token_map, _count_tokens, directory_tree, debug = prep_res
    if route in ("direct", "deterministic"):
        return route

    dir_groups = defaultdict(list)
    for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
        dir_groups[os.path.dirname(path)].append((i, path, content, file_token_map[i]))

    batches = []
    for dirname in sorted(dir_groups.keys()):
        current_batch = []
        current_tokens = 0
        for i, path, content, tokens in dir_groups[dirname]:
            if current_batch and (current_tokens + tokens > effective_limit or len(current_batch) >= batch_size):
                batches.append(current_batch)
                current_batch = []
                current_tokens = 0
            current_batch.append((i, path, content))
            current_tokens += tokens
        if current_batch:
            batches.append(current_batch)

    self._directory_tree = directory_tree
    return batches

The algorithm groups files by their parent directory (os.path.dirname(path)) so that related source modules remain together within the same batch. When appending a file would breach the effective token limit or the maximum file count cap (batch_size), the batch is finalized and a new batch initialized.

@staticmethod
def _build_directory_tree(files_data):
    """Build a compact directory tree string from the list of (path, content) tuples."""
    from collections import defaultdict

    dir_files = defaultdict(list)
    for i, (path, _content) in enumerate(files_data):
        dirname = os.path.dirname(path) or "."
        basename = os.path.basename(path)
        dir_files[dirname].append(f"{basename} (idx:{i})")

    lines = []
    for dirname in sorted(dir_files.keys()):
        lines.append(f"{dirname}/")
        lines.extend(f"  {fname}" for fname in sorted(dir_files[dirname]))
    return "\n".join(lines)

Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple

Description: Iteratively packs file contents up to 95% of the model context limit, building the file context and formatted listing for prompt insertion.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Pipeline shared state.

Returns: * tuple: Context string, file listing, file count, and prompt configuration parameters.

Example: 

def prep(self, shared):
    files_data = shared["files"]
    project_name = shared["project_name"]
    language = shared.get("language", "english")
    use_cache = shared.get("use_cache", True)
    max_abstraction_num = shared.get("max_abstraction_num", 10)
    thinking_level = shared.get("thinking_level", None)

    def create_llm_context(files_data):
        max_tokens = resolve_max_tokens(shared)
        safety_limit = int(max_tokens * 0.95)
        count_tokens = create_token_counter()
        context = ""
        file_info = []
        current_tokens = 0
        for i, (path, content) in enumerate(files_data):
            entry = f"--- File Index {i}: {path} ---\n{content}\n\n"
            entry_tokens = count_tokens(entry)
            if current_tokens + entry_tokens > safety_limit:
                print(f"\033[93mWarning: Context truncated at file index {i} ({path}) to fit within limit of {safety_limit} tokens.\033[0m")
                break
            context += entry
            file_info.append((i, path))
            current_tokens += entry_tokens
        return context, file_info

    context, file_info = create_llm_context(files_data)
    file_listing_for_prompt = "\n".join([f"- {idx} # {path}" for idx, path in file_info])
    return (context, file_listing_for_prompt, len(files_data), project_name, language, use_cache, max_abstraction_num, thinking_level, shared.get("advanced_mode", False), shared.get("max_tokens", 100000), shared.get("mode", "tutorial"))

The nested create_llm_context function ensures strict safety budgeting. Files are incorporated in sequential order until adding another file would exceed the 95% ceiling, at which point truncation warning logs are printed and appending ceases.

def exec(self, prep_res):
    try:
        # ... unpacks prep_res and prepares prompt ...
        prompt_template = load_prompt_template("identify_abstractions", mode=doc_mode)
        prompt = prompt_template.format(project_name=project_name, context=context, language_instruction=language_instruction, max_abstraction_num=max_abstraction_num, name_lang_hint=name_lang_hint, desc_lang_hint=desc_lang_hint, file_listing_for_prompt=file_listing_for_prompt)
        response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)
        abstractions = parse_yaml_response(response)

        validated_abstractions = []
        for item in abstractions:
            # ... validates keys and string types ...
            validated_indices = []
            for idx_entry in item["file_indices"]:
                idx_str = str(idx_entry).split("#")[0].strip()
                if "-" in idx_str:
                    parts = idx_str.split("-")
                    if len(parts) == 2:
                        start_idx = int(re.findall(r"\d+", parts[0])[0])
                        end_idx = int(re.findall(r"\d+", parts[1])[0])
                        validated_indices.extend(idx for idx in range(start_idx, end_idx + 1) if 0 <= idx < total_files_count)
                        continue
                nums = re.findall(r"\d+", idx_str)
                if nums and 0 <= int(nums[0]) < total_files_count:
                    validated_indices.append(int(nums[0]))
            item["files"] = sorted(set(validated_indices))
            validated_abstractions.append({"name": item["name"], "description": item["description"], "files": item["files"]})
        return validated_abstractions
    except Exception as e:
        llm_logger.error(f"[Node {self.__class__.__name__}] Error: {e}", exc_info=True)
        raise e

Visibility: Public Signature: def prep(self, shared: dict) -> tuple

Description: Allocates file snippet context token budgets evenly across all abstractions, redistributing unused capacity in a second pass before rendering snippet prompts.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared memory state.

Returns: * tuple: Formatted context snippets, abstraction index listings, abstraction count, and LLM arguments.

Example: 

def prep(self, shared):
    abstractions = shared["abstractions"]
    files_data = shared["files"]
    # ... builds header context and calculates total_budget ...
    per_abstr_budget = total_budget // max(num_abstractions, 1)
    included_indices = set()
    abstr_results = []

    # Pass 1: give each abstraction an equal share, track unused
    for _i, sized in enumerate(abstr_file_data):
        budget = per_abstr_budget
        included_files, remaining_files = [], []
        for idx, path, file_content, tokens in sized:
            if idx in included_indices:
                included_files.append((idx, path, None, 0))
                continue
            if tokens <= budget:
                included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                budget -= tokens
                included_indices.add(idx)
            else:
                remaining_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
        abstr_results.append((included_files, remaining_files, budget))

    # Pass 2: redistribute unused budget to abstractions that need more
    total_unused = sum(r[2] for r in abstr_results)
    if total_unused > 0:
        for i, (included_files, remaining_files, _unused) in enumerate(abstr_results):
            if not remaining_files or total_unused <= 0:
                continue
            for idx, path, file_content, tokens in list(remaining_files):
                if tokens <= total_unused:
                    included_files.append((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
                    total_unused -= tokens
                    included_indices.add(idx)
                    remaining_files.remove((idx, path, file_content, tokens))
    # ... builds context string and returns ...

The two-pass allocation prevents early abstractions in the list from monopolizing prompt context tokens. Files that are already included by previous abstractions are marked with path-only references (already shown above), eliminating redundant payload duplication.

Visibility: Public Signature: def exec(self, prep_res: tuple) -> list

Description: Calls the LLM to determine chapter sequencing and verifies that the returned list contains a full, non-duplicate permutation of abstraction indices.

Parameters: * prep_res (tuple): Unpacked tuple from prep().

Returns: * list: Ordered list of abstraction indices ([int, ...]).

Raises: * ValueError: If returned indices contain duplicates, are out of bounds, or omit any abstraction.

Example: 

def exec(self, prep_res):
    try:
        # ... unpacks prep_res, loads order_chapters template, and calls LLM ...
        response = call_llm(prompt, use_cache=(use_cache and self.cur_retry == 0), thinking_level=thinking_level)
        ordered_indices_raw = parse_yaml_response(response)

        ordered_indices = []
        seen_indices = set()
        for entry in ordered_indices_raw:
            idx = int(entry.split("#")[0].strip()) if isinstance(entry, str) else int(entry)
            if not (0 <= idx < num_abstractions):
                raise ValueError(f"Invalid index {idx} in ordered list. Max index is {num_abstractions - 1}.")
            if idx in seen_indices:
                raise ValueError(f"Duplicate index {idx} found in ordered list.")
            ordered_indices.append(idx)
            seen_indices.add(idx)

        if len(ordered_indices) != num_abstractions:
            raise ValueError(f"Ordered list length ({len(ordered_indices)}) does not match abstractions count ({num_abstractions}).")

        return ordered_indices
    except Exception as e:
        llm_logger.error(f"[Node {self.__class__.__name__}] Error: {e}", exc_info=True)
        raise e

Visibility: Public Signature: def post(self, shared: dict, prep_res: list, exec_res_list: list) -> None

Description: Aggregates all generated chapter texts into shared["chapters"], writes updated MD5 content hashes to .doc_cache_manifest.json if incremental mode is active, and cleans up temporary instance variables.

Parameters: * shared (dict): Shared dictionary. * prep_res (list): Prep batch inputs. * exec_res_list (list): Collection of execution results.

Example: 

def post(self, shared, prep_res, exec_res_list):
    import json, os
    shared["chapters"] = [res["content"] for res in exec_res_list]

    if shared.get("incremental"):
        output_dir = os.path.join(shared.get("output_dir", "output"), shared.get("project_name"))
        os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)
        manifest_path = os.path.join(output_dir, ".doc_cache_manifest.json")
        manifest = {}
        if os.path.exists(manifest_path):
            try:
                with open(manifest_path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    manifest = json.load(f)
            except Exception:
                pass
        for res in exec_res_list:
            if res.get("hash") and res.get("name"):
                manifest[res["name"]] = res["hash"]
        with open(manifest_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(manifest, f, indent=2)

    del self.chapters_written_so_far
    del self.chapter_summaries

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The utils.call_llm module provides an abstraction layer for interacting with Large Language Model (LLM) APIs across multiple backend providers. It handles model routing, parameter configuration, request construction, response parsing, error mitigation, response caching, and execution logging.

The module supports two primary pathways: 1. Google Gemini Native API (google-genai SDK): Leverages Vertex AI or direct API key authentication, supporting structured thinking budgets via ThinkingConfig for models such as gemini-3.7-flash. 2. OpenAI-Compatible Providers (OpenRouter, Ollama, etc.): Connects via HTTP REST requests to /v1/chat/completions endpoints, mapping provider-specific configuration variables and dynamically configuring reasoning effort or thinking budgets where supported.

In addition to inference routing, utils.call_llm implements local disk caching via llm_cache.json to prevent redundant network invocations during development and multi-stage workflow execution. It also provisions an isolated logger (llm_logger) configured with a NullHandler at import time and initialized into structured per-run log files on demand.

flowchart TD
    Start([call_llm invocation]) --> TokenCount[Count prompt tokens with token_utils]
    TokenCount --> CacheCheck{use_cache == True?}
    CacheCheck -- Yes --> LoadCache[load_cache from llm_cache.json]
    LoadCache --> CacheHit{Prompt in cache?}
    CacheHit -- Yes --> ReturnCache[Log and return cached response]
    CacheHit -- No --> ResolveProvider[Resolve provider via get_llm_provider]
    CacheCheck -- No --> ResolveProvider

    ResolveProvider --> ProviderBranch{Provider?}

    subgraph GeminiPathway [Google Gemini Backend]
        ProviderBranch -- GEMINI --> InitGeminiClient[Initialize genai.Client with API Key / Vertex]
        InitGeminiClient --> CheckGeminiThinking{thinking_level set?}
        CheckGeminiThinking -- Yes --> SetGeminiBudget[Configure ThinkingConfig budget]
        CheckGeminiThinking -- No --> ExecGemini[client.models.generate_content]
        SetGeminiBudget --> ExecGemini
        ExecGemini --> FilterParts[Extract text parts from candidate response]
    end

    subgraph GenericPathway [OpenAI-Compatible Provider Backend]
        ProviderBranch -- Other: OLLAMA / OPENROUTER --> BuildHeaders[Construct headers and JSON payload]
        BuildHeaders --> CheckRouterThinking{Provider and thinking_level?}
        CheckRouterThinking -- OPENROUTER --> CheckRouterCap[_get_openrouter_model_info]
        CheckRouterCap --> SetRouterEffort[Set reasoning.effort and temperature]
        CheckRouterThinking -- OLLAMA --> SetOllamaEffort[Set think and reasoning_effort]
        CheckRouterThinking -- None / Other --> PostRequest[HTTP POST to /v1/chat/completions]
        SetRouterEffort --> PostRequest
        SetOllamaEffort --> PostRequest
        PostRequest --> ParseResponse[Validate JSON and extract choices.0.message.content]
    end

    FilterParts --> SaveCacheCheck{use_cache == True?}
    ParseResponse --> SaveCacheCheck
    SaveCacheCheck -- Yes --> WriteDisk[save_cache to llm_cache.json]
    SaveCacheCheck -- No --> ReturnResponse([Return response text])
    WriteDisk --> ReturnResponse

docs.title: configure_logging()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def configure_logging(project_name: str = "project", mode: str = "tutorial") -> str:

Description: Initializes file-based logging for an active execution run. It resolves the output directory from the LOG_DIR environment variable (defaulting to logs), creates the directory if absent, sanitizes the project_name string to remove filesystem-unsafe characters, replaces dashes in mode, and constructs a timestamped log path. It purges all existing handlers (including NullHandler) on logger, attaches an explicit logging.FileHandler using UTF-8 encoding, and writes initial session metadata.

Parameters: * project_name (str, optional): The name of the project being processed, used to prefix the log file name. Defaults to "project". * mode (str, optional): The execution mode (e.g., "tutorial", "deep-dive"), used in the log file name. Defaults to "tutorial".

Returns: * str: The absolute or relative path to the created log file (logs/{safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{YYYYMMDD_HHmmss}.log).

Raises: * OSError: If the log directory cannot be created or the log file cannot be opened for writing.

Example: 

# Implementation from utils/call_llm.py
def configure_logging(project_name="project", mode="tutorial"):
    """Configure file-based logging for this run.

    Creates a new log file per invocation:
        logs/{project_name}_{mode}_{YYYYMMDD_HHmmss}.log

    Must be called from main() after parsing CLI arguments.
    """
    log_directory = os.getenv("LOG_DIR", "logs")
    os.makedirs(log_directory, exist_ok=True)

    # Sanitize project name for filesystem safety
    safe_project = "".join(c if c.isalnum() or c in "-_." else "_" for c in project_name)
    safe_mode = mode.replace("-", "_")
    timestamp = datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
    log_file = os.path.join(log_directory, f"{safe_project}_{safe_mode}_{timestamp}.log")

    # Remove any existing handlers (e.g., NullHandler) and add the file handler
    logger.handlers.clear()
    file_handler = logging.FileHandler(log_file, encoding="utf-8")
    file_handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s"))
    logger.addHandler(file_handler)

    # Log run metadata at the start of every log file
    logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")
    logger.info(f"RUN STARTED | project={project_name} | mode={mode} | timestamp={timestamp}")
    logger.info(f"Log file: {log_file}")
    logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")

    return log_file

The function provides complete separation between standard root logging and the LLM execution trace. By calling logger.handlers.clear(), it prevents duplicate log entries if configure_logging is invoked multiple times during test runs or pipeline restarts. The log format adheres to %(asctime)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s, and the opening banner guarantees traceability for run parameters and timestamps.

Visibility: Public Signature: def get_llm_provider() -> str | None:

Description: Determines the active LLM backend provider based on ambient environment variables. It reads LLM_PROVIDER; if this variable is unset but either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY is present in the environment, it defaults the provider value to "GEMINI".

Parameters: * None.

Returns: * str | None: The identified provider name (such as "GEMINI", "OLLAMA", or "OPENROUTER"), or None if no relevant environment variables are set.

Raises: * No exceptions raised.

Example: 

# Implementation from utils/call_llm.py
def get_llm_provider():
    provider = os.getenv("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if not provider and (os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID") or os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY")):
        provider = "GEMINI"
    # if necessary, add ANTHROPIC/OPENAI
    return provider

This resolution logic enables zero-config operation for Google Gemini users who only export GEMINI_API_KEY or GEMINI_PROJECT_ID in their environment or .env file. For other third-party providers like Ollama or OpenRouter, the user must explicitly declare LLM_PROVIDER=OLLAMA or LLM_PROVIDER=OPENROUTER.

    if _openrouter_models_cache is None:
        try:
            resp = requests.get("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models", timeout=5)
            _openrouter_models_cache = resp.json().get("data", [])
        except Exception:
            _openrouter_models_cache = []

    return next((m for m in _openrouter_models_cache if m.get("id") == model_id), None)

The function implements lazy network initialization and memoization. On first invocation, it queries OpenRouter's endpoint with a 5-second timeout. Subsequent queries across different pipeline nodes reuse the cached payload in _openrouter_models_cache, preventing unnecessary HTTP calls and avoiding rate limits during reasoning capability checks.

docs.title: get_model_context_length()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:

Description: Calculates or retrieves the maximum input context window size (in tokens) for a given endpoint and model identifier. If the endpoint corresponds to Gemini (or the model name includes "gemini"), it returns 1000000. If the endpoint belongs to OpenRouter, it queries the OpenRouter API to read the context_length field. If the model is not recognized or an error occurs, it falls back to a safe default of 100000.

Parameters: * endpoint_url (str): The base URL or target API endpoint. * model_name (str): The identifier of the model being evaluated. * api_key (str, optional): The API key for authenticated lookups. Defaults to "".

Returns: * int: The maximum token limit supported by the model context window.

Raises: * No exceptions are propagated; errors are logged via logger.warning and fallback values are returned.

Example: 

# Implementation from utils/call_llm.py
def get_model_context_length(endpoint_url: str, model_name: str, api_key: str = "") -> int:
    """
    Fetch the maximum context length of a model based on the endpoint.
    If endpoint is Gemini API, safely default to 1,000,000 tokens.
    If endpoint is openrouter.ai, make GET to /api/v1/models and extract.
    Default to 100,000.
    """
    default_limit = 100000
    try:
        if not endpoint_url:
            return default_limit

        if "generativelanguage.googleapis.com" in endpoint_url or "gemini" in model_name.lower():
            # Safely default to 1M tokens for Gemini models
            return 1000000

        if "openrouter.ai" in endpoint_url:
            resp = requests.get("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models", timeout=5)
            data = resp.json().get("data", [])
            for m in data:
                if m.get("id") == model_name:
                    return m.get("context_length", default_limit)
    except Exception as e:
        logger.warning(f"Failed to fetch context length for {model_name} at {endpoint_url}: {e}")

    return default_limit

This utility ensures downstream token-packing and prompt-chunking operations allocate context safely. By defaulting Google Gemini models to 1,000,000 tokens and checking dynamic OpenRouter context limits, it avoids context window overflow errors during large codebase crawl ingestions.

docs.title: _call_llm_provider()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Executes an HTTP POST request against an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions API endpoint configured via environment variables. It resolves {provider}_MODEL, {provider}_BASE_URL, and {provider}_API_KEY based on LLM_PROVIDER. For OpenRouter models supporting reasoning, it validates requested thinking_level values against supported_efforts and configures payload parameters (reasoning.effort and temperature=1.0). For Ollama, it maps thinking_level to both think and reasoning_effort.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The full text prompt to transmit to the model. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning effort level (e.g., "low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The textual completion returned under choices[0].message.content.

Raises: * ValueError: If required environment variables (LLM_PROVIDER, <provider>_MODEL, <provider>_BASE_URL) are missing, if invalid JSON is returned, or if the choices key is omitted from the response. * Exception: Wraps requests.exceptions.HTTPError, requests.exceptions.ConnectionError, requests.exceptions.Timeout, or generic requests.exceptions.RequestException with descriptive connection context.

Example: 

# Implementation excerpt from utils/call_llm.py
def _call_llm_provider(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    // ...
    # Read the provider from environment variable
    provider = os.environ.get("LLM_PROVIDER")
    if not provider:
        raise ValueError("LLM_PROVIDER environment variable is required")

    model_var = f"{provider}_MODEL"
    base_url_var = f"{provider}_BASE_URL"
    api_key_var = f"{provider}_API_KEY"

    model = os.environ.get(model_var)
    base_url = os.environ.get(base_url_var)
    api_key = os.environ.get(api_key_var, "")

    if not model:
        raise ValueError(f"{model_var} environment variable is required")
    if not base_url:
        raise ValueError(f"{base_url_var} environment variable is required")

    url = f"{base_url.rstrip('/')}/v1/chat/completions"
    headers = {"Content-Type": "application/json"}
    if api_key:
        headers["Authorization"] = f"Bearer {api_key}"

    payload = {
        "model": model,
        "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": prompt}],
        "temperature": 0.7,
    }

    if provider == "OPENROUTER" and thinking_level:
        model_info = _get_openrouter_model_info(model)
        if model_info and "reasoning" in model_info:
            supported_efforts = model_info["reasoning"].get("supported_efforts", [])
            if thinking_level.lower() in supported_efforts:
                payload["reasoning"] = {"effort": thinking_level.lower()}
                payload["temperature"] = 1.0
            else:
                logger.warning(f"Invalid thinking level '{thinking_level}' for model {model}. Supported efforts: {supported_efforts}")
        else:
            logger.warning(f"Model {model} does not support reasoning via OpenRouter API.")

    elif provider == "OLLAMA" and thinking_level:
        payload["think"] = thinking_level.lower()
        payload["reasoning_effort"] = thinking_level.lower()
        payload["temperature"] = 1.0

    try:
        response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=(10, 300))
        // ...
        response.raise_for_status()
        return response_json["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
    except requests.exceptions.HTTPError as e:
        // ...
        raise Exception(error_message) from e

The function handles timeouts using a tuple (10, 300), specifying a 10-second connection timeout and a 300-second read timeout to accommodate long reasoning generation cycles. It performs defensive assertions on the status code and JSON payload structure, checking for HTTP 200 responses that wrap API error blocks missing choices.

docs.title: _call_llm_gemini()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private Signature: def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: Invokes the Google GenAI SDK (google.genai.Client) using either Vertex AI credentials (GEMINI_PROJECT_ID and GEMINI_LOCATION) or direct API key authentication (GEMINI_API_KEY). It sets the target model via GEMINI_MODEL (defaulting to gemini-3.7-flash). If thinking_level is specified, it maps the level string (low, medium, high) to an explicit token budget (1024, 4096, 8192) inside types.ThinkingConfig and passes it to types.GenerateContentConfig. Finally, it concatenates and returns all non-null text parts from the response candidates.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The text prompt to process. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Reasoning level string ("low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The concatenated text string generated by the Gemini model. Returns "" if no candidates or text parts exist.

Raises: * ValueError: If neither GEMINI_PROJECT_ID nor GEMINI_API_KEY is present in the environment. * google.genai.errors.APIError: If the Google GenAI backend encounters quota, permission, or execution errors.

Example: 

# Implementation from utils/call_llm.py
def _call_llm_gemini(prompt: str, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    if os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"):
        client = genai.Client(vertexai=True, project=os.getenv("GEMINI_PROJECT_ID"), location=os.getenv("GEMINI_LOCATION", "us-central1"))
    elif os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"):
        client = genai.Client(api_key=os.getenv("GEMINI_API_KEY"))
    else:
        raise ValueError("Either GEMINI_PROJECT_ID or GEMINI_API_KEY must be set in the environment")
    model = os.getenv("GEMINI_MODEL", "gemini-3.7-flash")

    kwargs = {"model": model, "contents": [prompt]}

    if thinking_level:
        # Map string levels to budgets for the installed SDK version
        budget_map = {"low": 1024, "medium": 4096, "high": 8192}
        budget = budget_map.get(thinking_level.lower(), 4096)
        thinking_config = types.ThinkingConfig(include_thoughts=True, thinking_budget=budget)
        kwargs["config"] = types.GenerateContentConfig(thinking_config=thinking_config)

    response = client.models.generate_content(**kwargs)

    # Extract only text parts to avoid "non-text parts: ['thought_signature']" warnings
    if response.candidates and response.candidates[0].content.parts:
        text_parts = [part.text for part in response.candidates[0].content.parts if part.text is not None]
        return "".join(text_parts)
    return ""

This method filters out non-textual parts (such as thought_signature or raw reasoning trace structures) emitted by reasoning-capable Gemini models, preventing SDK warnings or formatting artifacts in generated documentation. It dynamically handles both Google Cloud Vertex AI infrastructure deployments and standalone developer API keys.

docs.title: call_llm()
docs.text:
Visibility: Public Signature: def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:

Description: The primary entrypoint function for executing LLM completion requests within the application. It counts prompt tokens using utils.token_utils.count_tokens, checks and reads the disk cache (llm_cache.json) when use_cache is True, dispatches the request to either _call_llm_gemini or _call_llm_provider, tracks request latency, writes new responses back to cache if enabled, and emits detailed timing and execution metrics to logger.

Parameters: * prompt (str): The full text prompt string. * use_cache (bool, optional): Whether to inspect and write to llm_cache.json. Defaults to True. * thinking_level (str | None, optional): Optional reasoning budget identifier ("low", "medium", "high"). Defaults to None.

Returns: * str: The textual response generated by the model or retrieved from disk cache.

Raises: * ValueError: If provider environment configuration is missing or invalid. * Exception: If upstream API calls fail or connection errors occur.

Example: 

# Implementation from utils/call_llm.py
def call_llm(prompt: str, use_cache: bool = True, thinking_level: str | None = None) -> str:
    import time

    from utils.token_utils import count_tokens

    provider = get_llm_provider()
    model = os.environ.get(f"{provider}_MODEL", os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL", "unknown"))
    prompt_tokens = count_tokens(prompt)

    logger.info(f"{'=' * 80}")
    logger.info(
        f"LLM CALL START | provider={provider} | model={model} | thinking={thinking_level} | cache={'enabled' if use_cache else 'disabled'} | prompt_tokens={prompt_tokens:,}"
    )
    logger.info(f"PROMPT:\n{prompt}")

    # Check cache if enabled
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        if prompt in cache:
            cached_response = cache[prompt]
            logger.info(f"CACHE HIT | response_chars={len(cached_response):,}")
            logger.info(f"RESPONSE (cached):\n{cached_response}")
            logger.info("LLM CALL END | result=cache_hit")
            return cached_response

    # Make the actual LLM call
    start_time = time.time()
    logger.info(f"API CALL | sending request to {provider}...")

    if provider == "GEMINI":
        response_text = _call_llm_gemini(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)
    else:  # generic method using a URL that is OpenAI compatible API (Ollama, ...)
        response_text = _call_llm_provider(prompt, thinking_level=thinking_level)

    elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    logger.info(f"API CALL COMPLETE | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s | response_chars={len(response_text):,}")
    logger.info(f"RESPONSE:\n{response_text}")

    # Update cache if enabled
    if use_cache:
        cache = load_cache()
        cache[prompt] = response_text
        save_cache(cache)
        logger.info("CACHE WRITE | saved response to cache")

    logger.info(f"LLM CALL END | result=success | elapsed={elapsed:.1f}s")
    return response_text

The function serves as the central orchestration point for all LLM calls in the pipeline. It ensures consistent logging of prompts, character counts, elapsed network execution time, and token usage across both cached and non-cached requests.

docs.text:
utils/crawl_github_files.py

Following the LLM execution utilities documented in utils.call_llm, this module provides repository extraction utilities for fetching source files directly from GitHub. It serves as an ingestion mechanism for remote codebases, retrieving files and directory structures across branches, tags, specific commits, or subdirectories.

docs.title: Technical Overview
docs.text:
The utils.crawl_github_files module ingests source code from remote GitHub repositories through two distinct retrieval strategies:

  1. SSH Git Clone Strategy: When provided an SSH URL (starting with git@ or ending with .git), the module clones the repository into a temporary directory via git.Repo.clone_from. It then parses .gitignore rules with pathspec.PathSpec and performs a local filesystem walk.
  2. GitHub REST API Strategy: When provided an HTTPS repository URL, the module parses repository components (owner, repo, branch/tree ref, and specific subdirectory path) via urllib.parse.urlparse. It queries GitHub's REST API endpoints (/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents, /branches, and /git/trees), automatically handles rate limits (403/429 with X-RateLimit-Reset backoff), resolves .gitignore rules, and recursively crawls files and subdirectories.

docs.text:
Visibility: Private (nested helper within crawl_github_files) Signature: def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec: pathspec.PathSpec | None = None) -> bool:

Description: Evaluates whether a candidate file matches the active inclusion patterns, passes .gitignore path specification rules, and is not rejected by explicit exclusion patterns.

Parameters: * file_path (str): Relative file path from the repository or target subdirectory root. * file_name (str): Base filename (used for fnmatch matching against include_patterns). * gitignore_spec (pathspec.PathSpec | None, optional): Compiled gitignore path specification. Defaults to None.

Returns: * bool: True if the file passes all inclusion, gitignore, and exclusion checks; False otherwise.

Implementation Logic: 

    def should_include_file(file_path: str, file_name: str, gitignore_spec=None) -> bool:
        """Determine if a file should be included based on patterns"""
        # If no include patterns are specified, include all files
        if not include_patterns:
            include_file = True
        else:
            # Check if file matches any include pattern
            include_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_name, pattern) for pattern in include_patterns)

        # Check gitignore if provided
        if include_file and gitignore_spec and gitignore_spec.match_file(file_path):
            return False

        # If exclude patterns are specified, check if file should be excluded
        if exclude_patterns and include_file:
            # Exclude if file matches any exclude pattern
            exclude_file = any(fnmatch.fnmatch(file_path, pattern) for pattern in exclude_patterns)
            return not exclude_file

        return include_file

The filtering algorithm applies a three-stage filter. First, if include_patterns is populated, the base file_name must match at least one glob pattern using fnmatch.fnmatch. Second, if a compiled gitignore_spec exists and matches the file_path, the candidate is immediately rejected. Third, if exclude_patterns is present, the full file_path is evaluated against each pattern; any match results in rejection.

Example: 

# Invocation inside crawl_github_files during traversal:
if not should_include_file(rel_path, filename, gitignore_spec=gitignore_spec):
    count_excluded += 1
    print(f"{C_GRAY}  [{entry_num}] {rel_path} [excluded]{C_RESET}")
    continue

docs.text:
Visibility: Private (nested helper within crawl_github_files) Signature: def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str) -> list[dict]:

Description: Retrieves the list of active branch objects for the target repository via the GitHub REST API (/repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches). Handles unauthenticated rate limits and repository access errors.

Parameters: * owner (str): GitHub repository owner (user or organization). * repo (str): GitHub repository name.

Returns: * list[dict]: List of branch dictionaries returned by the GitHub API, or an empty list [] if the request fails or is unauthorized.

Raises: * Exception: If GitHub API rate limits (HTTP 403 or 429) are encountered and no authorization token was supplied.

Implementation Logic: 

    def fetch_branches(owner: str, repo: str):
        """Get brancshes of the repository"""

        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches"
        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and not token:
            raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")

        if response.status_code == 404:
            if not token:
                print(
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or is private.\n"
                    "If this is a private repository, please provide a valid GitHub token via the 'token' argument or set the GITHUB_TOKEN environment variable."
                )
            else:
                print(
                    "Error 404: Repository not found or insufficient permissions with the provided token.\n"
                    "Please verify the repository exists and the token has access to this repository."
                )
            return []

        if response.status_code != 200:
            print(f"Error fetching the branches of {owner}/{repo}: {response.status_code} - {response.text}")
            return []

        return response.json()

The function executes a requests.get call targeting the repository branches endpoint with a 30-second connect/read timeout. If an HTTP 403 or 429 error occurs in the absence of a PAT token, it raises an explicit exception alerting the caller to rate limits. When encountering 404 responses, it prints diagnostic guidance distinguishing between private repository visibility and permission failures before returning an empty list.

Example:

branch_names = (branch.get("name") for branch in branches)

# Fetching branches is not successfully

if ref is None:

docs.title: fetch_contents()
docs.text:
Visibility: Private (nested helper within crawl_github_files) Signature: def fetch_contents(path: str) -> None:

Description: Recursively navigates GitHub repository directory structures at a specific path and commit reference. Downloads raw text content for matching files and traverses child directories.

Parameters: * path (str): Subdirectory or file path within the repository to fetch.

Returns: * None: Mutates the enclosing files, skipped_files, and api_counters state structures.

Raises: * Exception: If unauthenticated rate limits are encountered.

Implementation Logic: 

    def fetch_contents(path):
        """Fetch contents of the repository at a specific path and commit"""
        url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}"
        params = {"ref": ref} if ref is not None else {}

        response = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params, timeout=(30, 30))

        if response.status_code in (403, 429) and "rate limit exceeded" in response.text.lower():
            if not token:
                raise Exception("GitHub API rate limit exceeded. Please provide a GitHub token using --token or GITHUB_TOKEN env var.")
            reset_time = int(response.headers.get("X-RateLimit-Reset", 0))
            wait_time = max(reset_time - time.time(), 0) + 1
            print(f"Rate limit exceeded. Waiting for {wait_time:.0f} seconds...")
            time.sleep(wait_time)
            return fetch_contents(path)

        # ... Directory recursion and file download logic ...

When fetch_contents encounters authenticated rate limits (HTTP 403/429), it calculates the remaining wait time from the X-RateLimit-Reset HTTP header, sleeps using time.sleep, and retries the request recursively. For each returned item, if type == "dir", it checks directory exclusion rules before initiating recursive calls. If type == "file", it validates size thresholds and attempts to fetch raw file contents via download_url, falling back to base64 decoding of the content field if download_url is unavailable.

Example: 

    # Start crawling from the specified path
    fetch_contents(specific_path)

docs.text:
The utils.crawl_local_files module provides local filesystem traversal and content extraction capabilities for the Codebase-Knowledge-Builder repository. Its primary responsibility is scanning a target directory on disk, applying hierarchical exclusion and inclusion filters (including native .gitignore rules via pathspec), enforcing file size thresholds, decoding text files safely with UTF-8 BOM awareness, and returning an in-memory mapping of relative file paths to their textual contents.

This module acts as the local counterpart to utils.crawl_github_files, adhering to an identical output contract {"files": {filepath: content}}. This unified data structure feeds directly into downstream graph nodes (such as those defined in nodes and executed within flow) for AST parsing, token budget estimation, and LLM prompt generation.
